Medication assistance record entries for each dose
Refusal and prescriber notification notes
Written orders and confirmation of telephone orders
1-business-day primary physician notification note
PRN orders and consultation notes
Authorized staff list and training and competency records
Advanced HHA registry check, in-service hours, RN assessment, patient-specific instructions and RN visit log
Monthly audit results

policies.title: Nursing Services, Home Care Agency Arrangements and Delegation (EALR/SNALR Nursing Coverage)
policies.applies_to: ALR, EALR and SNALR (including enriched housing and adult home programs); ALP participants
policies.purpose: To make sure residents get the nursing and health services they need through lawful arrangements and that EALR and SNALR nursing coverage meets state minimums.
policies.policy: A basic ALR at [AGENCY NAME] arranges needed nursing, home health aide, therapy, social work, nutrition and supply services through an Article 36 home care agency. A home care agency may not provide basic adult home or enriched housing services such as personal care unless it is under contract to do so and those services are in the basic rate (10 NYCRR 1001.10(k)(2)-(3)). Residents may use providers with whom the operator has no arrangement and may choose their own health care providers (1001.10(e)-(f)). In an EALR or SNALR, the facility staffs an RN on site 8 hours a day, 5 days a week, and an LPN 8 hours a day on the other 2 days. An RN is on call 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, when not on site, with added coverage when the medical evaluation or ISP requires it (1001.11(j)). A facility with 40 beds or fewer may ask DOH for a written waiver, which takes effect only on DOH's written approval and must be disclosed to residents (1001.11(k)-(l)). Aging in place in the EALR follows Public Health Law 4655.

definitions.definition: A home care services agency licensed or certified under Article 36 of the Public Health Law.
Enhanced Assisted Living Residence, certified to allow aging in place with added nursing and aide services.
Special Needs Assisted Living Residence, certified to serve residents with special needs such as dementia.
A home health aide on the home care worker registry who performs RN-assigned advanced tasks under direct RN supervision.
Written DOH approval, available to operators of 40 beds or fewer, to vary the RN/LPN on-site schedule; effective only on DOH's written approval.

procedures: At admission and each annual reassessment, the Case Manager lists each resident's nursing, home health aide, therapy and other health service needs in the ISP and identifies who will provide each (see ARD-02, ARD-03).

For services that [AGENCY NAME] does not provide itself, the Administrator arranges them through an Article 36 home care agency. The written arrangement states who provides which services, response times, communication and the agency contact, and is signed by both parties.

The Administrator checks that any home care agency under contract does not provide basic adult home or enriched housing services (such as personal care) unless the contract says so and the basic rate covers them. Contracts are reviewed annually.

Tell each resident, in the admission agreement and at admission, that they may use providers [AGENCY NAME] has no arrangement with and may choose their own health care providers. Staff never pressure a resident to use a specific provider (see RR-01, RR-04).

For an outside provider, the Case Manager shares the ISP and medication information with the provider (with the resident's consent), coordinates visit schedules and records the visit and any changes in the record.

EALR/SNALR: the Administrator builds the staffing schedule so an RN is on site 8 hours a day, 5 days a week, and an LPN is on site 8 hours a day on the other 2 days. Posted schedules show the RN on call for every hour not covered on site.
EALR/SNALR: the Administrator keeps a current on-call roster with the RN's name and 24-hour phone number [PHONE] and tests it quarterly. Staff know how to reach the RN at any hour.
If the resident medical evaluation or ISP calls for more nursing time, the Administrator increases coverage and documents the added hours.

Waiver: a facility with 40 beds or fewer that wants a waiver submits a written request to DOH. The waiver is not used until DOH approves it in writing. The Administrator then discloses the waiver to current and prospective residents in writing and files the approval and disclosures.

When an RN is not on site, the Administrator schedules enough home health aides trained in first aid and medication assistance to meet resident needs, and verifies each aide's training records (see STF-04).
Home health aides complete 12 hours of annual in-service. The Administrator tracks hours and dates for each aide (see STF-03).

Before an RN assigns an advanced task to an advanced home health aide, the RN completes a nursing assessment and medication review of the resident and writes patient-specific instructions. The RN keeps these in the record and reviews them when the resident's condition changes.
Advanced home health aides are verified on the home care worker registry, complete 18 hours annual in-service, and receive direct RN supervision, with an RN visit at least every 2 weeks (see HCS-02).

For EALR residents who age in place, the Administrator obtains and files the physician's report required under Public Health Law 4655 and re-checks that nursing coverage meets the resident's needs (see ARD-04).
If a resident needs 24-hour skilled nursing, the Administrator applies ARD-04: the resident is discharged unless all four conditions in 10 NYCRR 1001.10(m)(5) are met.
The Administrator reviews nursing coverage logs, contracts and delegation records quarterly and reports to the QA/QI Committee (see GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Arranges and reviews home care agency contracts, builds compliant RN/LPN schedules, requests and discloses any waiver, and keeps the on-call roster.
Provides on-site and on-call coverage, assesses residents, delegates and supervises advanced tasks with written instructions, and documents visits.
Covers on-site hours on the days the RN is not scheduled, within scope of practice.
Identifies service needs in the ISP, coordinates with outside providers and tracks resident choice of provider.
Complete required training and in-service and perform only tasks they are authorized and instructed to do.

documentation: ISP service plan showing who provides each service
Signed home care agency contracts and annual review notes
Resident choice-of-provider acknowledgement
RN/LPN schedules and on-call roster
DOH waiver request, written approval and resident disclosure (if applicable)
Aide training, first aid, medication assistance, in-service and registry records
RN nursing assessments, medication reviews and patient-specific instructions
RN supervisory visit log
Physician's report for aging in place
Quarterly nursing coverage review

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
policies.applies_to: Adult Home / Enriched Housing Program with ALR, EALR and SNALR licensure; ALP participants
policies.purpose: To make sure staff recognize and respond to changes in a resident's condition, notify physicians and families promptly, transfer residents safely, and share information across shifts.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] responds immediately to any change in a resident's condition. If a resident cannot or will not eat regular meals for 2 consecutive days, staff immediately notify the personal physician, act on the instructions given and note the call in the record (18 NYCRR 487.7(d)(5)). On illness or injury, staff protect the resident, obtain emergency help, transfer the resident if necessary, and notify the personal physician (or qualified alternate) and the representative or next of kin (487.7(d)(6)). Staff send the approved transfer form (or the medical evaluation and personal data sheet) and any requested information with the resident. For emergency transfers, staff phone the information and send written information within 72 hours. Where dangerous behavior occurs, staff arrange professional evaluation, transfer if necessary, and notify the representative or next of kin (487.7(d)(7)). Weights are taken and recorded monthly. A resident is not admitted or readmitted from a hospital or skilled nursing facility without a referral statement (487.4(o)).

definitions.definition: A sudden or gradual change in a resident's physical, mental, behavioral or functional status, including illness, injury, weight change, refusal of meals or medication, or new dangerous behavior.
The physician the resident has chosen for primary care, or that physician's qualified alternate.
The DOH-approved form, or the medical evaluation and personal data sheet, sent with a resident being transferred.
A statement from a hospital or skilled nursing facility that supports the resident's admission or return to the facility.

procedures: Any staff member who sees a change of condition stays with the resident if there is any danger, calls 911 if the situation is an emergency, and tells the supervisor on duty at once.

For illness or injury, staff protect the resident from further harm, give first aid within their training, and obtain emergency help. The supervisor decides on transfer, calling 911 whenever there is doubt.

The supervisor notifies the resident's personal physician (or qualified alternate) as soon as possible and follows the physician's instructions. The call, time, person spoken to and instructions are written in the resident record.
The supervisor notifies the resident's representative or next of kin as soon as possible, and records the time and the person reached. The Administrator and Case Manager are told the same day.

If a resident does not eat regular meals for 2 consecutive days, the staff member who notices tells the supervisor, and the supervisor immediately calls the personal physician, follows the instructions, and notes the call and instructions in the record. Meal intake is tracked daily on the meal intake sheet until stable.

Staff take each resident's weight monthly, record it on the weight record, and report any significant change to the Case Manager or RN within one business day for physician notification. Staff re-weigh as directed.

For a hospital transfer, staff send with the resident the approved transfer form (or the medical evaluation and personal data sheet), the current medication list and any other information requested by the receiving provider.

For an emergency transfer, a staff member phones the receiving provider with the required information and then sends the written information within 72 hours. The date, time and person spoken to are recorded.
Staff record the event in the resident record: what happened, who was notified, when, what was done, where the resident was sent and how.

If a resident shows dangerous behavior toward self or others, staff keep everyone safe, remove others from danger where possible, and notify the supervisor. The supervisor arranges a professional evaluation, transfers the resident if necessary, and notifies the representative or next of kin. Restraints are not used (see SAF-04).
Complete an incident report for any injury, hospital transfer, dangerous behavior or other reportable event during the same shift and follow SAF-02 for reporting to the state.

Use a shift report or communication log so incident and change-of-condition information reaches all shifts. The outgoing supervisor briefs the incoming supervisor at every shift change, and the log is initialed.

The Case Manager follows up within one business day of any change of condition: updates the ISP, asks for a new medical evaluation if the change may affect retention (see ARD-04), and informs the RN in an EALR/SNALR.

Before a resident returns from a hospital or skilled nursing facility, the Case Manager obtains the referral statement, discharge orders and medication list, and the Administrator confirms that the resident still meets retention criteria. Do not accept the resident back without the referral statement.
If the return is not appropriate, the Administrator follows ARD-04 and ARD-05, including notices and placement efforts.
The Administrator reviews transfers and change-of-condition events each quarter for trends and reports them to the QA/QI Committee (see GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the system for notifying physicians and families and sharing information across shifts works, reviews all hospital transfers, and decides on readmission.
Directs the response to a change of condition, calls the physician and family, authorizes transfer and completes the transfer information.
Follows up on changes, updates the ISP, reviews weights and obtains referral statements and discharge information.
Observe and report changes in condition immediately, take monthly weights and record meal intake.

documentation: Resident record notes on each change of condition and physician and family notifications
Meal intake sheet and record of 2-day notification
Monthly weight record
Transfer form or medical evaluation and personal data sheet copy
72-hour written follow-up for emergency transfers
Incident reports
Shift communication log

Quarterly transfer trend report

policies.title: Dementia and Special Needs Assisted Living (SNALR) Memory Care
policies.applies_to: All residents with dementia or other cognitive impairment, and all staff. Programmatic provisions apply only if [AGENCY NAME] holds SNALR certification and an approved special needs plan; mark N/A for the SNALR program if it does not.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] offers dementia-specific services only when it is certified and approved to do so, observes and supervises residents with dementia safely and without unlawful confinement, and meets the nursing coverage and medication limits that apply to special needs assisted living.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides dementia-specific services, and designates SNALR beds, only with Special Needs Assisted Living Residence (SNALR) certification and an approved special needs plan (10 NYCRR 1001.10(n); Public Health Law 4655). SNALR beds are located in a fixed, identified area of the building (10 NYCRR 1001.13). The program regularly observes and assesses each resident's service needs through a comprehensive, coordinated program, and maintains community linkages specific to the special-needs population (10 NYCRR 1001.10(n)). Staff always know the general whereabouts of each SNALR resident. If a resident is absent and their whereabouts are unknown, staff begin immediate efforts to locate the resident (10 NYCRR 1001.10(n)). No resident is ever locked in a room. Any secured-unit design or door-alarm or egress feature is cleared with the DOH Regional Office and architecture review before use. The nursing coverage rules for EALR/SNALR in 10 NYCRR 1001.11 apply. PRN prescription drugs for residents with dementia are limited as 10 NYCRR 1001.10 provides and are given only under HCS-01 and HCS-02. [AGENCY NAME] admits and retains a resident with dementia only while it can meet the resident's needs within its certification, the resident's individualized service plan, and the retention limits in ARD-04.

definitions.definition: A Special Needs Assisted Living Residence: an assisted living residence certified by DOH to serve residents with special needs, such as dementia, under an approved special needs plan.
The written plan approved by DOH describing how the SNALR will serve its special-needs population, including observation, assessment, supervision and community linkages.
The identified, defined portion of the building in which the SNALR beds are located.
A resident is absent from the building or expected location and staff cannot confirm where the resident is.
A medication ordered by a physician to be given 'as needed' under written conditions rather than on a fixed schedule.

procedures: Before the facility advertises, admits or designates any bed for dementia care, the Administrator confirms in writing that SNALR certification and the approved special needs plan are in effect, and files the certification and plan with GOV-03 licensure records.

The Administrator marks the SNALR beds on the facility floor plan and census. Only the fixed SNALR area is used for SNALR-designated beds. Any proposed change to the area is submitted to DOH before it is made.

At pre-admission, the case manager completes the screening and evaluation under ARD-01 and ARD-02. The case manager confirms with the resident's physician that the resident's cognitive status and behaviors can be served within the SNALR program and are not conditions listed in ARD-04.

The case manager develops the individualized service plan under ARD-03 with the resident, the resident's representative where applicable, and the physician. The plan states cognitive status, communication needs, wandering or exit-seeking risk, behaviors, preferred routines, and the interventions to be used.
The case manager reassesses each resident at least every 12 months and whenever there is a change in function or behavior. The ISP is updated after any identified change in function.

The Administrator and case manager run the program's observation and assessment process. Direct-care staff record behavioral and functional observations each shift on the [SNALR OBSERVATION LOG]. The case manager reviews the log at least weekly and acts on trends.

Every shift supervisor assigns staff to see each SNALR resident at the intervals set in the resident's ISP. At each shift change, outgoing staff tell incoming staff where each resident is and any concerns.
Staff maintain a census and location check of SNALR residents under SAF-09, including after meals, activities and any fire drill or alarm.

If a resident's whereabouts are unknown, the staff member who notices immediately alerts the shift supervisor. Staff begin an immediate search of the SNALR area, the building and the grounds, and the supervisor follows SAF-03 including notifications and incident reporting.

No staff member locks a resident in a bedroom or any other room. Staff do not use restraints or restrictive practices as defined in SAF-04. The Administrator submits any secured-unit or delayed-egress design for DOH Regional Office review and approval before installation and keeps fire safety consistent with SAF-06.

Nursing coverage follows HCS-03 and 10 NYCRR 1001.11: RN on site 8 hours per day, 5 days per week; LPN 8 hours per day on the other 2 days; and an RN on call 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The Administrator documents any DOH-approved waiver available for facilities of 40 or fewer beds and its conditions.

Medication staff give PRN prescription drugs to residents with dementia only as the physician's order and the limits of 10 NYCRR 1001.10 allow, and record each dose on the medication assistance record under HCS-01 and HCS-02. A PRN is never used to control behavior for staff convenience. The nurse or case manager notifies the physician if PRN use is frequent.

The Administrator arranges and maintains community linkages specific to the dementia population, such as the local Alzheimer's Association chapter, the area agency on aging, mental health and geriatric providers, and hospice. Each linkage is recorded on the [COMMUNITY LINKAGE LIST], which is reviewed at least annually.

Staff who work with SNALR residents receive orientation and training on dementia care, communication, behavior support, wandering and elopement response, and abuse prevention under STF-03. Attendance is recorded in the personnel file under STF-06.
The case manager informs family or representatives of the program, the resident's observed changes and any incident, consistent with RR-07 on confidentiality.
The QA/QI Committee reviews SNALR elopement events, incidents, falls, PRN use and transfers at least quarterly under GOV-05.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains SNALR certification and the special needs plan, keeps SNALR beds in the fixed area, ensures required nursing coverage, and oversees the program.
Screens, assesses and reassesses residents, develops the ISP, reviews observation logs and coordinates with physicians and families.
Provides nursing coverage as required, reviews PRN use with physicians and advises staff on health-related care.
Observe and record resident behavior, know each resident's whereabouts, and begin immediate search efforts if a resident is missing.
Directs location checks and handoffs and starts missing-resident response.

documentation: SNALR certification and approved special needs plan
Floor plan marking the fixed SNALR area
Pre-admission screening, evaluations, and annual reassessments
Individualized service plans and updates
[SNALR OBSERVATION LOG] and case manager review notes
Medication assistance records showing PRN use
Incident reports for missing residents or injuries
Staff training records and nursing coverage schedules

policies.title: Falls Prevention
policies.applies_to: All residents, and all direct-care, nursing, case management, housekeeping and maintenance staff.
policies.purpose: To reduce the risk of falls and fall-related injuries, and to make sure falls and injuries are promptly responded to, reported, investigated and used to update resident service plans.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] works to prevent falls through supervision, monitoring for changes in behavior or appearance, a working emergency call system, a safe environment and individualized service planning. Staff monitor residents for abrupt or progressive changes in behavior or appearance and monitor the emergency call system (18 NYCRR 487.7(d)). A resident who is injured or has an accident, on or off the grounds, that requires medical attention is reported on Incident Report DSS-3123 (18 NYCRR 487.7(d)). After an identified change in function, the individualized service plan is revised (10 NYCRR 1001.10(g)). The regulations do not prescribe a fall-risk tool or specific interventions, so [AGENCY NAME] uses the facility-defined procedures below. These are applied consistently and reviewed by the QA/QI Committee. The call system in bedrooms, toilets and baths is kept in working order (18 NYCRR 487.11).

definitions.definition: An unintended event in which a resident comes to rest on the floor, ground or a lower surface, whether or not an injury results and whether or not it was witnessed.
The facility-defined [FALL RISK SCREEN] completed by the case manager or nurse to identify residents at risk, based on history, mobility, medications, vision, cognition, continence and environment.
The resident call system installed in bedrooms, toilets and baths that alerts staff to a resident's request for help.
A noticeable decline or alteration in a resident's mobility, balance, cognition, continence, behavior or ability to perform activities of daily living.

procedures: At pre-admission and annual evaluation (ARD-01, ARD-02), the case manager records the resident's fall history, mobility aids, balance problems, vision, medications that may contribute to falls, continence and cognition, and completes the [FALL RISK SCREEN].
The case manager rescreens each resident at least every 12 months, after any fall, after any hospital or rehabilitation stay, and when staff report a change in function or behavior.

For a resident at risk, the case manager writes specific fall-prevention interventions into the individualized service plan (ARD-03) and tells all shifts. Examples include supervised walking, mobility aids, footwear, night lighting, a bed or toilet location near the call device, and scheduled toileting assistance.

Direct-care staff observe residents each shift for abrupt or progressive changes in behavior or appearance, such as new unsteadiness, confusion, dizziness, weakness or pain. They report any change to the shift supervisor immediately and record it in the resident's notes.
The shift supervisor reports changes in condition under HCS-04, informs the physician, and tells the next shift at handoff.

The case manager or nurse arranges for the resident's physician or a home care agency (HCS-03) to review medications that may increase fall risk. Dose changes are made only with physician authorization, as described in HCS-01.
Staff record each resident's weight monthly as part of personal care and report unexplained loss or gain to the case manager, since weight changes can reflect declining strength or health.

Maintenance staff test the call system in each bedroom, toilet and bath at least monthly and after any repair, record the results on the [CALL SYSTEM TEST LOG], and repair failures immediately or provide alternative monitoring until the repair is complete (see SAF-09 and DL-03).
Staff monitor the call system around the clock and respond to each call promptly. Any recurring delay in response is reported to the Administrator.

Housekeeping and maintenance staff keep hallways, stairs, bathrooms and common areas free of clutter, spills, loose cords and uneven surfaces, clean up spills immediately, and report hazards on the [HAZARD REPORT].

If a resident falls, the nearest staff member stays with the resident, does not move the resident if injury is suspected, calls for the nurse or shift supervisor, and summons emergency services (911) if there are signs of serious injury, head injury, or the resident cannot get up safely.

The shift supervisor checks the resident, notifies the physician and the resident's representative, and records the circumstances, injuries and actions taken. A resident who has a head strike or takes anticoagulant medication is closely monitored per the physician's direction.

If the resident is injured or the fall requires medical attention, on or off the grounds, the shift supervisor completes Incident Report DSS-3123 and submits it under SAF-02 and REC-02. The Administrator or case manager investigates the incident the next business day.

Within 72 hours of any fall, the case manager reviews the cause, updates the fall risk screen and revises the ISP when there is an identified change in function. Changes are communicated to all shifts.
The Administrator reports falls monthly to the QA/QI Committee, including trends by location, time of day, resident and shift. The Committee recommends corrective actions under GOV-05.
If a resident's falls cannot be reduced and the resident needs continual medical or nursing care, the case manager refers the resident for evaluation under ARD-04.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the call system works, supports fall-prevention staffing and supplies, investigates serious falls, and reports trends to QA/QI.
Completes fall risk screens, writes and updates service plan interventions, and reviews each fall.
Reviews medications and health factors that contribute to falls, and advises staff and physicians.
Observe residents, respond promptly to calls, assist with mobility, and report changes and falls.
Keep the environment hazard-free and the call system working.

policies.title: Skin Integrity and Pressure Injury Prevention
policies.applies_to: All residents, and all direct-care, nursing, case management and housekeeping staff.
policies.purpose: To prevent skin breakdown through personal care and observation, to report skin changes promptly, and to refer residents whose wound or skin needs exceed what [AGENCY NAME] may lawfully provide.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] protects residents' skin through personal care, including bathing, toileting, ordinary movement from bed to chair and monthly weights (18 NYCRR 487.7(e)), and through supervision and observation for changes. Changes in a resident's condition are reported to all shifts and to the physician (18 NYCRR 487.7(d), (e)). Residents whose condition is unstable and requires continual skilled observation, or who are chronically bedfast, may not be retained (18 NYCRR 487.4). Wounds or skin treatments beyond the facility's scope are referred to an Article 36 licensed home care agency or other qualified provider (10 NYCRR 1001.10). No skin-specific regulation was verified, so [AGENCY NAME] relies on these personal care, supervision and referral duties and on the facility-defined procedures below. Staff do not perform skilled wound care or treatments outside their authorized role.

definitions.definition: Localized damage to skin or underlying tissue, usually over a bony area, caused by pressure or pressure with friction or shear.
A visual look at a resident's skin, including bony areas and skin folds, performed during personal care.
A resident who is confined to bed on a long-term basis and cannot be retained under the admission standards.
Care of open wounds or pressure injuries that requires licensed nursing assessment or treatment and is provided only by qualified licensed providers, such as a home care agency.

procedures: At pre-admission and annual evaluation (ARD-01, ARD-02), the case manager records skin condition, existing wounds, mobility, continence, nutrition, and any physician orders for skin care. An applicant who has unstable conditions requiring continual skilled observation or who is chronically bedfast is not admitted (ARD-04).

The case manager identifies residents at higher risk for skin breakdown, such as those with limited mobility, incontinence, poor nutrition or hydration, or prior pressure injury, and writes preventive measures into the individualized service plan (ARD-03).

Direct-care staff observe skin during bathing, dressing and toileting, and look at bony areas, heels and skin folds. They report redness that does not fade, open areas, blisters, bruising, swelling, pain or drainage to the shift supervisor the same shift.
Staff assist residents with ordinary movement from bed to chair, encourage position changes and walking as tolerated, and assist with toileting on the schedule in the ISP.
Staff keep residents clean and dry, and promptly assist after incontinence. Incontinence that is chronic and unmanaged is reported to the case manager for review under ARD-04.

Dietary staff and the case manager encourage adequate fluids and nutrition under DL-01, and staff report poor intake. Staff record weights monthly and report unplanned weight change to the case manager.
Housekeeping staff keep bedding and clothing clean, dry and wrinkle-free, and report soiled or damaged mattresses, cushions or heel protectors to the Administrator.

The shift supervisor reports any new skin change to the physician and the resident's representative (HCS-04), records it in the resident's notes, and tells all shifts at handoff so the change is monitored.

Staff do not cut, debride or dress open wounds, apply prescription treatments they are not authorized to apply, or give injections. They may help a resident apply a physician-ordered topical product only within HCS-02 limits.

If a resident has a wound or skin condition that requires skilled care, the case manager arranges for treatment by an Article 36 home care agency or another qualified provider chosen by the resident, and documents responsibilities in the ISP (HCS-03, HCS-08).

The case manager re-evaluates retention after any pressure injury or skin treatment need. If the resident's needs require continual skilled observation, or the resident has become chronically bedfast, the case manager and Administrator start the retention review and discharge planning in ARD-04 and ARD-05, with persistent efforts at alternative placement.
After a hospital or rehabilitation stay, the case manager obtains discharge orders, inspects the resident's skin on return, and updates the ISP before the resident resumes normal routines.
If a skin injury or wound is suspected to result from neglect, staff report it immediately to the Administrator, who follows SAF-01.
The Administrator reviews skin integrity events, including new pressure injuries and referrals, and reports them quarterly to the QA/QI Committee (GOV-05).
Direct-care staff receive training on skin observation, repositioning, incontinence care and reporting at orientation and at least annually (STF-03, STF-04), documented in the personnel file.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures supplies and staffing support skin protection, oversees retention decisions, and reports trends to QA/QI.
Identifies risk, writes the plan, coordinates physician and home care referrals, and re-evaluates retention.
Perform personal care, check skin, reposition and assist, and report all changes.
Reports changes to the physician and representative, and communicates across shifts.
Provides skilled wound assessment and treatment as the ISP and physician orders specify.

Individualized service plans with prevention measures
Resident notes documenting skin changes and notifications

Training records

policies.title: Hospice and Home Care Agency Coordination
policies.applies_to: Residents receiving hospice or home care agency services, and the Administrator, case manager and care staff.
policies.purpose: To coordinate safely with hospice and licensed home care agencies so residents receive needed services while [AGENCY NAME] keeps its own responsibility for residence services.
policies.policy: Residents may use outside providers and choose their own health care providers. Home care services in the residence are provided only by an Article 36 licensed home care agency (10 NYCRR 1001.10). Hospice is allowed in an assisted living residence without EALR certification if [AGENCY NAME], the resident's physician and the hospice agree the resident can be safely cared for, responsibilities are written into the individualized service plan, and the operator agrees to retain the resident and coordinate care (10 NYCRR 1001.10). [AGENCY NAME] remains responsible for adult home or enriched housing basic services even if a contracted home care agency fails to provide its services (10 NYCRR 1001.10). The case manager coordinates with the outside providers the resident chooses (10 NYCRR 1001.10).

definitions.definition: A home care agency licensed or certified under Article 36 of the Public Health Law, such as a LHCSA or CHHA.
A program of palliative and supportive care for terminally ill residents and their families, provided by a licensed hospice agency.
The written agreement or coordination between the facility and a home care agency describing who provides which services to residents.
The room, board, housekeeping, supervision, personal care, case management and activities that the operator must provide.

procedures: When a resident or representative requests hospice or home care, the case manager records the request and informs the resident that they may choose among licensed providers, including their own, and are not required to use a provider of the facility's choosing.
Before any home care agency provides services in the residence, the case manager verifies and records that the agency is an Article 36 agency, copying the license or certificate to the file.

The Administrator signs a written coordination or service agreement with each home care agency that regularly serves residents. The agreement states how the agency communicates with the facility, who provides each service, the agency's staff identification and access procedure, and emergency contact numbers.

For a resident requesting hospice, the case manager convenes the resident or representative, the resident's physician, the hospice agency and the Administrator to decide whether the resident can be safely cared for in the residence.

If all parties agree, the Administrator confirms in writing that [AGENCY NAME] agrees to retain the resident and to coordinate care. If any party disagrees, the case manager records the reasons, explains alternatives to the resident, and reviews retention under ARD-04.

The case manager writes the responsibilities of the facility, hospice, home care agency and resident or representative into the ISP, including personal care, medication assistance, symptom reporting, equipment, and emergency steps (ARD-03).

Facility staff and hospice or home care staff exchange information at each visit or as the ISP requires. Facility staff report observed changes to the case manager and to the agency, and the case manager records them.
The case manager reviews the ISP with the hospice or home care team at least when the resident's condition changes, and updates it after any identified change in function.

Medications brought or ordered by hospice are handled under HCS-01 and HCS-02. Facility staff do not give injections or take on tasks beyond their authorized role, and hospice or home care staff provide those services.

If a home care agency fails to provide scheduled services, the case manager contacts the agency the same day, arranges a replacement or back-up plan, and ensures the resident's basic services continue without interruption. The Administrator keeps facility staff on duty to meet adult home or enriched housing basic services at all times.

The case manager records each missed visit or failure, tells the resident's physician and representative where health is at risk, and gives the Administrator a report. Repeated failures are reported to the QA/QI Committee, and the Administrator considers whether the agency agreement should continue.

Where a resident declines in condition and the hospice team believes care needs exceed what can be provided in the residence, the case manager follows ARD-04 and ARD-05 and makes persistent efforts toward alternative placement only if the resident and hospice agree it is needed.
If a hospice resident dies, staff follow HCS-09 and coordinate with the hospice agency on notification and post-death procedures.
The Administrator reviews agency agreements and coordination at least annually and records the review in the agency file.

responsibilities.duty: Signs agency agreements, agrees to retain hospice residents when appropriate, and ensures basic services continue if an agency fails.
Verifies agency licensure, coordinates with providers the resident chooses, and writes responsibilities into the ISP.
Provide residence services, observe and report changes, and cooperate with agency staff.
Provides the services listed in the ISP and agreement and communicates changes.

documentation: Copies of agency licenses or certificates
Written agency coordination agreements
Hospice agreement documentation and retention decision
Individualized service plans listing responsibilities

policies.title: Death of a Resident
policies.applies_to: All staff. Specific duties rest with the shift supervisor, case manager and Administrator.
policies.purpose: To make sure a resident's death is handled with dignity, that required notifications and reports are made on time, and that the resident's money, property and records are handled lawfully.
policies.policy: When a resident dies, [AGENCY NAME] immediately notifies the next of kin or representative, if known, and the appropriate local authorities (18 NYCRR 487.7(d)). The facility immediately reports the death by telephone to the DOH Regional Office, and the Incident Report must be received by DOH within 24 hours (18 NYCRR 487.7(d)). If the resident ever received services from a mental hygiene service provider, a report to the Justice Center on its form must also be received within 24 hours (18 NYCRR 487.7(d)). An Incident Report is required whenever a resident dies, and the Administrator or case manager investigates incidents involving death (18 NYCRR 487.7(d)). The resident's money and property are returned to the representative with a final account (18 NYCRR 487.5(d)). Records are kept for the retention period required after death (see REC-01).

definitions.definition: The person designated by the resident, or authorized by law, to act for the resident, such as a health care agent, guardian or next of kin.
The DOH form used to report incidents, including a resident's death.
A provider of services under the Mental Hygiene Law, such as an OMH-, OPWDD- or OASAS-regulated program.
The written statement of the resident's funds and property held by the facility, showing all deposits, withdrawals, charges and the balance returned.

procedures: Staff who find a resident without signs of life call 911 immediately unless a valid DNR or MOLST order is on file, and follow RR-06. They start CPR if no such order exists and they are trained and authorized. They notify the shift supervisor at once.
The shift supervisor confirms the resident's code status from the chart, directs emergency response, and keeps other residents safe and informed in a respectful way.
The shift supervisor immediately notifies the resident's next of kin or representative, if known, by telephone, and records the time, person reached and message.

The shift supervisor immediately notifies the appropriate local authorities, such as law enforcement or the medical examiner or coroner as the circumstances and local procedure require. The supervisor also notifies the resident's physician and any hospice or home care agency involved.

The shift supervisor or Administrator immediately telephones the DOH Regional Office serving the facility: Capital District (518) 408-5287, Central NY (315) 477-8472, Western NY (585) 423-8188, or Metropolitan Area (212) 417-4440. After hours, the Administrator uses the DOH emergency contact on the posted list in REC-03 and records the time, person spoken to and any instructions.

The case manager or shift supervisor completes Incident Report DSS-3123 for the death, with facts only. The Administrator reviews it and ensures it is received by the DOH Regional Office within 24 hours of the death, and keeps proof of transmission.

The case manager checks the resident's record for any prior mental hygiene service provider. If the resident ever received such services, the Administrator ensures that the Justice Center report is prepared on its form and received by the Justice Center within 24 hours, and records the date and time of submission.
If the circumstances suggest abuse, neglect, exploitation or an unexplained injury, the Administrator also follows SAF-01 and preserves the scene, records and any evidence for investigators.

Staff protect the resident's privacy and dignity, keep the room secure, and release the body only to the funeral director, hospice or authority designated by the representative or required by law. Staff do not discuss the death with outsiders (RR-07).

Staff inventory the resident's room, money and personal property with a second staff member present, record the inventory, and secure the items. Funds held for the resident under RR-05 are reconciled.

The Administrator returns the resident's money and property to the representative, or to the person lawfully entitled to receive it, with a final account, and obtains a signed receipt. Any refund due under the admission agreement is calculated and returned under RR-04.

The Administrator or case manager investigates the circumstances of the death, interviews staff on duty, reviews the resident's ISP and recent changes in condition, and records findings and any corrective action within [NUMBER] business days.
The case manager informs other residents and staff sensitively, offers support, and informs the resident council if the family agrees. The Administrator offers staff support as needed.

The case manager closes the resident's record, notes the date of death, and retains it for the period required after death (REC-01). The Administrator updates the census and notifies any funding source, such as the social services district.
The Administrator brings the death and its review to the QA/QI Committee, with attention to patterns, response time and whether any care or safety changes are needed (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Directs emergency response and makes immediate notifications to the family, local authorities, physician and DOH.
Prepares the Incident Report and Justice Center report if required, inventories property, and closes the record.
Ensures reports are received on time, investigates the death, returns funds and property with a final account, and informs QA/QI.
Call for help, follow code status, protect dignity and privacy, and assist with the inventory.

documentation: Notification log with times and persons reached
Incident Report DSS-3123 and proof of receipt
Justice Center report and proof of receipt, if required
Property and money inventory, final account and signed receipt
Death investigation notes
Closed resident record with date of death
QA/QI Committee minutes

policies.title: Medicaid Assisted Living Program (ALP) Eligibility, Services and Staffing
policies.applies_to: Applies only if [AGENCY NAME] holds ALP approval under Social Services Law 461-l. Mark as N/A for private-pay-only operations. When it applies, it covers the Administrator, ALP designated individual, case manager, nursing, care staff and billing staff.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] operates the Medicaid Assisted Living Program only with proper approval, enrolls eligible residents, delivers the services covered by the capitated rate, and meets ALP staffing and wage requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates an ALP only with approval under Social Services Law 461-l, which requires a licensed home care services agency (LHCSA) or certified home health agency (CHHA) under identical ownership and approval of the Public Health and Health Planning Council (PHHPC). ALP residents receive the resident services and the services covered by the Medicaid capitated rate (18 NYCRR 494.5). The facility has a designated individual for the program, a qualified case manager, and at least the minimum staffing levels referred to in 18 NYCRR 494.6, which cross-refers to the supervision levels in 18 NYCRR 487.9(f)(6). Personal care staff must be trained for home care. Nursing and therapies are inside the capitated service package. People enrolled in the ALP are not eligible for managed long term care (Public Health Law 4403-f). ALP rates are provider-specific per diems set at 50% of low-intensity nursing home prices by wage-equalization region (Public Health Law 3614(6)). New ALP beds are approved case by case on public need.

definitions.definition: The Assisted Living Program: a Medicaid program under Social Services Law 461-l in which an adult home or enriched housing program provides a package of residence and home care services for a capitated rate.
The fixed Medicaid per diem paid to the ALP for each enrolled resident, set by DOH rate setting, which covers the services in the ALP package.
The person named as responsible for the ALP and its compliance with program requirements.
The resource utilization group classification, based on resident assessment, used to set the provider-specific per diem.
Medicaid managed long term care, which ALP residents may not join while enrolled in the ALP.

procedures: The Administrator confirms and keeps on file the written ALP approval, the PHHPC approval, and the license or certificate of the LHCSA or CHHA under identical ownership. The Administrator confirms the approved number of ALP beds and records any change.

The Administrator names the ALP designated individual and a qualified case manager, which means a registered nurse, a master's-level social worker, or a person with a degree and the required experience under 18 NYCRR 494.6. The Administrator keeps credentials, job descriptions and DOH notices on file under STF-06.

The Administrator sets ALP schedules to meet at least the supervision levels referenced in 18 NYCRR 494.6, at least one staff member on site at all times for a census of 1-40 and two for 41-80, plus the weekly hours per resident for personal care (3.75 hours), housekeeping (1.0 hour) and food service (2.0 hours). Schedules and census are checked against this each week under STF-01.

The case manager screens applicants for ALP enrollment after the pre-admission process in ARD-01 and ARD-02, and confirms that the applicant meets the ALP eligibility criteria of Social Services Law 461-l, as applied by DOH and the local social services district, before enrollment. Eligibility steps and decisions are recorded in the resident file.

The case manager confirms that the applicant is not enrolled in managed long term care. An ALP resident is not eligible for MLTC, so the case manager helps the applicant understand that enrollment choice and records the discussion in the file.

The case manager explains to the resident, in writing and in plain language, what the ALP package includes and what the resident's rights are under RR-01, including the right to choose among providers within the program's rules.

The case manager develops the ISP under ARD-03 and arranges the services covered in the capitated rate under 18 NYCRR 494.5, including personal care, nursing and therapies. Services are delivered by qualified staff, with each service, frequency and provider recorded in the ISP.
The Administrator ensures that personal care staff are trained for home care before assignment, with training and competency records kept under STF-03 and STF-06.

The case manager and nurse reassess each resident at least every 12 months and when function changes, and use the assessment for the RUG-II classification that supports the per diem. The assessment accurately reflects resident need and is never changed to affect payment.

Billing staff record services and enrolled days from the daily census and ISP and submit claims only for covered services actually delivered to enrolled residents, under GOV-06. The Administrator reviews billing before submission.

The Administrator checks the provider-specific per diem notice from DOH rate setting. The Administrator compares billed rates with the notice, which reflects the rate methodology of 50% of low-intensity nursing home prices by region. Questions are sent to the DOH rate-setting bureau at ALP-Rates@health.ny.gov.

The Administrator pays LHCSA home care aides at least the home care aide minimum wage in effect: $19.65 per hour in the downstate region and $18.65 elsewhere in 2026, rising to $20.00 and $19.00 on January 1, 2027, and checks payroll against this under STF-08.

Residents who no longer qualify for or need ALP services are given written notice and help with transition. The case manager follows ARD-04 and ARD-05 for retention and discharge and does not end enrollment without notice under those policies.

If [AGENCY NAME] seeks to add ALP beds, the Administrator confirms the current rules, including case-by-case review of new beds on public need since April 1, 2025, and any expedited review available to existing ALPs in good standing for a small number of added beds. The Administrator files the proper application with DOH and PHHPC before using any added beds.

The Administrator reviews ALP staffing, eligibility records, service delivery, billing and wages at least quarterly and reports findings to the QA/QI Committee (GOV-05). Any noncompliance is corrected and documented.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains ALP approvals, staffing, wage compliance and billing integrity, and reports on ALP operations to QA/QI.
Oversees program compliance and acts as the contact for DOH on the ALP.
Determines eligibility, confirms no MLTC enrollment, builds the ISP and reassesses residents.
Provide covered nursing and therapy services and support reassessment.
Submit accurate claims for covered services and reconcile to per diem notices.

Designated individual and case manager credentials
Staffing schedules and census records
ALP eligibility determinations and MLTC non-enrollment notes
ISPs, assessments and RUG-II classification records
DOH per diem notices, claims and reconciliations
Home care aide wage and payroll records

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting (Justice Center / DOH)
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers, contractors and the Administrator of the adult home / enriched housing program, ALR, EALR, SNALR and ALP
policies.purpose: To keep residents free from abuse, neglect and exploitation, and to make sure every suspected incident is reported to the correct authority on time, investigated, and documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] prohibits physical, mental and emotional abuse, neglect, and exploitation of residents, and does not require residents to give gratuities. Before opening, the Administrator will confirm with the NYS Department of Health (DOH) whether [AGENCY NAME] is a 'facility' as defined in the Social Services Law and is therefore subject to the Justice Center for the Protection of People with Special Needs. If it is, every mandated reporter must report a reportable incident to the Justice Center immediately on reasonable cause. The Justice Center must receive the report within 24 hours of discovery, including the names and contact details of all persons with knowledge. The facility will start an investigation, and the Justice Center and/or DOH may also investigate. The Administrator will investigate and report to DOH any allegation that would constitute a reportable incident. If the facility is not subject to the Justice Center, staff report to the Administrator, who reports to DOH and law enforcement as appropriate. A complaint or evidence of abuse always requires an Incident Report. Staff are never to wait for an investigation, a supervisor's approval or proof before reporting. No one may retaliate against a person who reports in good faith.

definitions.definition: An allegation or suspicion of abuse, neglect or exploitation of a resident that meets the Justice Center's definitions, which the facility must report when it is subject to the Justice Center.
A staff member or other person required by law to report a reportable incident immediately on reasonable cause.
Having a reason to suspect that abuse, neglect or exploitation may have occurred. Certainty is not required.
The DOH form used to document the incidents listed in 18 NYCRR 487.7(d)(11), including a complaint or evidence of resident abuse.
The NYS Justice Center for the Protection of People with Special Needs, which receives and investigates reportable incidents at covered facilities.

procedures: Before opening, the Administrator will ask DOH in writing whether [AGENCY NAME] is a facility subject to the Justice Center. The Administrator will file the written answer in the regulatory file and record the result in this policy.

If the facility is subject to the Justice Center, the Administrator will confirm the current Justice Center hotline number directly with the Justice Center before posting it. The Administrator will post it where residents, staff and visitors can see it, next to the grievance procedure, as [JUSTICE CENTER HOTLINE NUMBER – confirm current number before posting].

Any staff member, volunteer or contractor who witnesses, suspects or is told of possible abuse, neglect or exploitation will first make sure the resident is safe. The person will separate the resident from any alleged abuser, get medical care if needed, and preserve the scene and any evidence.

A mandated reporter will report a reportable incident to the Justice Center immediately on reasonable cause by calling the hotline. The report must reach the Justice Center within 24 hours of discovery. The reporter must not delegate the duty or wait for a supervisor's approval, and must give the names and contact details of all persons with knowledge.

The reporter will notify the Administrator or the supervisor on duty immediately after making the report. If the Administrator is the person alleged, the reporter will notify [GOVERNING BODY CONTACT] and the DOH regional office.

The Administrator will start an investigation immediately. The Administrator will protect the resident, interview witnesses, secure statements and records, and cooperate fully with the Justice Center, DOH and law enforcement. The Administrator will not interfere with their investigations.

The Administrator will report to DOH any allegation that would constitute a reportable incident. The Administrator will complete an Incident Report (DSS-3123) for every complaint or evidence of resident abuse and send a copy to the DOH regional office as described in SAF-02.

For a suspected felony against or by a resident, the Administrator will call the DOH regional office immediately. The Administrator will send the Incident Report within 24 hours and notify law enforcement within 24 hours. If the resident has ever received mental hygiene services, the Administrator will also send a Justice Center report within 24 hours.

The Administrator will remove an accused employee from resident contact, or place the employee on administrative leave, while the matter is investigated if resident safety requires it. The Administrator will keep this action separate from any finding of fault.

The Administrator will notify the resident's representative, next of kin or designated contact of the allegation and the steps taken, unless the resident objects. Where the resident objects, the Administrator will record that.

The Administrator will offer the resident medical evaluation, emotional support and, where wanted, access to the Ombudsman and to legal and advocacy services (see RR-03). The case manager will update the Individualized Service Plan if the resident's needs change.

The Administrator will review each completed investigation, decide on corrective and disciplinary action, and refer the event to the QA/QI Committee (see GOV-05) for trend review. The Administrator will report any substantiated staff findings as required and will check the Justice Center Staff Exclusion List as described in STF-02.

At hire, and before the employee has unsupervised resident contact, the Administrator or designee will train each employee on identifying reportable incidents, reporting procedures, and mandated reporter duties. The employee will sign the Justice Center code of conduct acknowledgment, and will re-sign it every year.

The Administrator will train volunteers and contractors who have resident contact on how to recognize and report abuse, using the same content in a shortened form. The Administrator will keep the training record.
The Administrator will conduct a review of this policy at least annually and after any substantiated incident, and will report the outcome to the governing body.

responsibilities.duty: Protect residents, report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately, and never retaliate against a reporter.
Report directly to the Justice Center immediately on reasonable cause, with the report received within 24 hours of discovery, when the facility is subject to the Justice Center.
Confirm Justice Center status with DOH, post the hotline, start and complete investigations, report to DOH, complete Incident Reports, train staff and review outcomes.
Support the affected resident, offer advocacy and legal service information, and update the Individualized Service Plan.
Receive reports on allegations and outcomes, and receive any allegation involving the Administrator.

documentation: Written DOH determination of Justice Center status
Posted hotline notice with date of posting and confirmation
Justice Center and DOH report confirmations with date and time
Incident Report DSS-3123 and the chronological Incident Report log
Investigation file: statements, evidence list, findings and corrective actions
Training records and signed annual Justice Center code of conduct acknowledgments
QA/QI Committee minutes showing trend review

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
policies.applies_to: All staff, supervisors and the Administrator in the adult home / enriched housing program, ALR, EALR, SNALR and ALP
policies.purpose: To make sure every reportable incident and accident is documented on the correct DOH form, reported to DOH and other authorities within the required timeframes, and used to improve resident safety.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will prepare an Incident Report (DSS-3123) whenever any of the following occurs: a resident's whereabouts are unknown for more than 24 hours; an assault or injury by or to a resident; a suicide attempt or a death; a complaint or evidence of resident abuse; behavior that impairs the well-being of others or interferes with operations; an accident on or off the grounds that requires medical attention; or a suspected felony. A copy goes in the resident's record. The Administrator keeps a chronological log of all Incident Reports showing the resident and incident type, and sends copies to the DOH regional office. Where the facility is subject to the Justice Center, the Administrator will also make the required Justice Center report (see SAF-01). Reports include the resident's version of events unless the resident objects. Reports about an employee are placed in that employee's personnel file.

definitions.definition: Form DSS-3123, the DOH-mandated form used to document incidents under 18 NYCRR 487.7(d)(11).
A chronological list of every Incident Report, showing the resident name and the type of incident.
The DOH regional office (Capital District, Central NY, Western NY or Metropolitan Area) that oversees [AGENCY NAME].
The first working day after the event, for the DOH notices required by 18 NYCRR 487.12(j).

procedures: The staff member who discovers or is told of an incident will first provide first aid or call 911 as needed and secure the resident's safety. The staff member will then notify the supervisor on duty and the Administrator.

The staff member who witnessed or discovered the incident will complete the Incident Report (DSS-3123) before the end of the shift. It will include the date, time, place, persons involved, witnesses, injuries, actions taken and notifications made.

The reporter will ask the resident for his or her account of what happened and will record it in the report unless the resident objects. If the resident objects, the reporter will write that the resident declined.
The supervisor on duty will review the report the same day and notify the resident's physician and representative as described in HCS-04.

For a death, the Administrator will notify the DOH regional office within 24 hours, following HCS-09. For an attempted suicide, the Administrator will notify DOH within 24 hours. For a suspected felony, the Administrator will call the regional office immediately and send the Incident Report and law enforcement notice within 24 hours.
If a resident's whereabouts are unknown for more than 24 hours, the Administrator will follow SAF-03, including the 5-working-day Incident Report deadline.
If the incident involves possible abuse, neglect or exploitation, the Administrator will follow SAF-01 for Justice Center reporting and investigation.

The Administrator will notify DOH by the next business day of a fire, work stoppage, loss of a fire system, no hot water, or interruption of essential services, using the regional office contact for [AGENCY NAME]: [REGIONAL OFFICE PHONE]. Regional offices are Capital (518) 408-5287, Central (315) 477-8472, Western (585) 423-8188, and Metropolitan Area (212) 417-4440.
The Administrator will review, sign and date every Incident Report within one working day, and will confirm that the notifications required for that incident type were made.

The Administrator will place a copy of the report in the resident's record and enter it in the chronological Incident Report log. The Administrator will send copies to the DOH regional office as required.
If the incident involves an employee, the Administrator will place a copy in the employee's personnel file and take any follow-up action under STF-07.
The case manager will review the resident's Individualized Service Plan after each incident and update it if needed, for example for falls or behavior changes.
The Administrator will give the QA/QI Committee a summary of incidents by type, time, location and cause at every meeting, and the Committee will recommend corrective actions (see GOV-05).
The Administrator will check at least quarterly that every incident in the log has a matching report, that every required notification was made on time, and that follow-up was completed.

responsibilities.role: Staff member who discovers the incident
responsibilities.duty: Ensure the resident's safety, notify the supervisor, and complete the Incident Report before end of shift.
Review the report the same day and make physician and representative notifications.
Make DOH, law enforcement and Justice Center notifications on time, sign reports, keep the log, send copies, and report to the QA/QI Committee.
Review and update the Individualized Service Plan after incidents.
Review incident trends and recommend corrective action.

documentation: Completed Incident Reports (DSS-3123) with Administrator signature and date
Chronological Incident Report log with resident and incident type
Copies sent to the DOH regional office with transmission proof
Resident record copy and personnel file copy where applicable
Record of notifications to physician, representative, law enforcement and Justice Center
Quarterly log audit and QA/QI Committee minutes

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
policies.applies_to: All staff, supervisors and the Administrator in the adult home / enriched housing program, ALR, EALR, SNALR and ALP
policies.purpose: To make sure staff know each resident's general whereabouts, respond quickly when a resident cannot be found, and make all required notifications, while respecting residents' right to come and go and live in the community.
policies.policy: Supervision at [AGENCY NAME] includes knowing each resident's general whereabouts and recording a daily census on the DOH form (DSS-2900). If a resident's whereabouts are unknown, staff will start efforts to find the resident at once. If the absence exceeds 24 hours, the Administrator will immediately notify the resident's next of kin or representative and law enforcement, notify the DOH regional office on the first available working day, and send the Incident Report to the regional office within 5 working days. Residents are not locked in and may take part in community life as they prefer, with recognition of safety. Staff will not use locks, restraints or other restrictions to prevent a resident from leaving. The SNALR program has its own, stricter immediate-search requirements, which are carried out under HCS-05 in addition to this policy.

definitions.definition: A resident is not where expected, has not signed out or told staff of plans, and staff cannot confirm where the resident is.
The daily record of resident presence on DOH form DSS-2900.
A resident who is cognitively impaired or at risk leaving the premises without staff knowing and without safe arrangements.
The system by which a resident tells staff when leaving, where he or she is going and the expected return time.

procedures: The staff member on duty will record the daily census on DSS-2900 at the time set by the Administrator ([CENSUS TIMES]) and will check that every resident is accounted for at each shift change.

Residents who go out will be asked, but not required, to tell staff where they are going and when they expect to return. The sign-out will be kept voluntary and will not be used to limit a resident's freedom to leave.

The case manager will identify residents at risk of wandering or elopement during assessment and service planning (see ARD-02 and ARD-03), and will list individualized supervision measures in the Individualized Service Plan.

When a resident is not where expected and not accounted for, the staff member will notify the supervisor on duty immediately and begin a search of the resident's room, common areas, grounds, and likely places in the community the resident is known to visit.

The supervisor will assign staff to search by area and will keep enough staff in the building to supervise the other residents. The supervisor will call the resident's known contacts and check with hospitals if there is reason to think the resident was taken ill.

The supervisor will notify the Administrator as soon as the resident is found to be missing, and the Administrator will decide whether to call 911 immediately. Staff will call 911 at once if the resident is cognitively impaired, medically fragile, or the circumstances suggest danger, and will not wait for 24 hours to pass.

If the resident is not located and the absence exceeds 24 hours, the Administrator will immediately notify the resident's next of kin or representative and law enforcement. The Administrator will give law enforcement a recent description, photograph, medical conditions and medications.
The Administrator will notify the DOH regional office on the first available working day, using [REGIONAL OFFICE PHONE].

The Administrator will complete the Incident Report (DSS-3123) and send it to the DOH regional office within 5 working days. The Administrator will also place a copy in the resident's record and enter it in the Incident Report log (see SAF-02).
If the circumstances suggest abuse, neglect or a suspected felony, the Administrator will also follow SAF-01 and the 24-hour notice requirements in SAF-02.

When the resident is found or returns, staff will check the resident for injury and illness, notify the physician where needed, and tell the representative and law enforcement that the resident has returned.
The case manager will meet with the resident, within [NUMBER] days of return, to learn why the resident left and review risks. The case manager will update the Individualized Service Plan.
If the resident wishes to leave permanently, the Administrator will follow RR-04 and ARD-05 and will not hold the resident against his or her wishes.
The Administrator will review each missing-resident event with the QA/QI Committee to identify any gaps in supervision, census practice, or service planning (see GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Keep the daily census, notice absences, begin the search at once and notify the supervisor.
Direct the search, maintain coverage for other residents and notify the Administrator.
Call 911 where indicated, make the 24-hour and working-day notifications, complete and send the Incident Report, and review the event.
Identify residents at risk and update the Individualized Service Plan.

documentation: Daily census on DSS-2900
Search log: times, areas searched, staff and contacts made
Record of notification to next of kin or representative, law enforcement and DOH regional office
Incident Report (DSS-3123) with date sent to the regional office
Resident record entry and Individualized Service Plan update
QA/QI Committee minutes

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
policies.applies_to: All staff, supervisors, nursing and case management staff and the Administrator in the adult home / enriched housing program, ALR, EALR, SNALR and ALP
policies.purpose: To protect residents from physical and chemical restraint, seclusion and confinement, and to give staff approved, less restrictive ways to respond to distress and unsafe behavior.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not use physical restraints. A physical restraint is any apparatus that prevents free movement of the arms or legs or immobilizes a resident who cannot remove it. Residents are free from coercion and restraint, and are never restrained in any way or locked in a room. Residents are not confined to their room or bed except during short-term illness, and any use of a sick bay is limited under the regulations. Staff may not change a resident's medication dose or schedule without physician authorization, and medication is never used to control or sedate a resident for staff convenience. Use of PRN psychotropic medication for a resident with dementia is restricted under the SNALR regulations and requires physician direction as described in HCS-05. Any staff member who uses or proposes a restraint is subject to discipline under STF-07 and the matter will be handled under SAF-01.

definitions.definition: Any apparatus that prevents free movement of the arms or legs, or immobilizes a resident who cannot remove it. Examples include vests, belts, wrist or ankle ties, locked or tied chairs and bedrails used to keep a resident in bed.
Use of medication to control or sedate a resident when it is not required to treat a diagnosed medical condition and has not been ordered by a physician.
Locking a resident in a room or keeping a resident in his or her room or bed against the resident's will.
A designated space used for short-term care of ill residents, with use limited under the regulations.

procedures: The Administrator will confirm that no physical restraint devices, such as vests, belts, ties or tray-locked chairs, are kept or used in the building, and will check this at each monthly environmental review.

The Administrator will confirm that no door is locked to prevent a resident from leaving a room or the building, except as permitted for fire and building security without keeping residents in. Where a SNALR secured unit exists, it operates under HCS-05.

Staff will respond to distress, agitation or unsafe behavior with approved de-escalation steps. These include speaking calmly, reducing noise and stimulation, finding and removing the trigger, offering food, toileting or pain relief, redirecting to an activity, and calling the supervisor.

If a resident's behavior puts that resident or others in immediate danger, staff will move other residents away, stay with the resident from a safe distance, call the supervisor, and call 911 or the crisis service if danger continues. Staff will never tie, hold down or lock in the resident.

A resident will not be kept in his or her room or bed except during short-term illness, and then only at the resident's request or on physician advice. The supervisor will record the reason and review it at every shift.

Staff will not give, withhold, or adjust any medication dose or time to control behavior. Staff will call the resident's physician for any medication change and will make the change only on physician authorization (see HCS-01 and HCS-02).

For residents with dementia, staff will not give PRN psychotropic medication unless it is ordered and meets the restrictions that apply to SNALR; the nurse or supervising clinician will check the order before it is given (see HCS-05).

Staff will report any witnessed or suspected restraint, seclusion, confinement or inappropriate medication use to the supervisor immediately. The Administrator will treat it as a possible abuse allegation under SAF-01 and complete an Incident Report under SAF-02.

The case manager will evaluate any resident who repeatedly presents with unsafe behavior and, with the resident's physician, a mental health provider and the resident or representative, will develop an individualized plan to address causes without restraint (see ARD-03).
If [AGENCY NAME] cannot safely meet a resident's needs without restraint or confinement, the Administrator will apply ARD-04 and ARD-05 and will help arrange a more suitable placement.
The Administrator will train all staff on this policy at orientation and annually, and will keep the training record (see STF-03).
The QA/QI Committee will review any restraint allegation, behavior incident or medication-related concern at each meeting (see GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Never use restraint, seclusion or confinement, use de-escalation, and report any suspected use at once.
Direct response to unsafe behavior, call 911 or the physician, and notify the Administrator.
Verify medication orders and PRN use, and assist in behavior planning.
Develop individualized, non-restrictive plans for residents with recurring behaviors.
Ensure no restraint devices are present, investigate allegations, train staff and report to the QA/QI Committee.

documentation: Monthly environmental check noting absence of restraint devices
Incident Reports for any behavior event or restraint allegation
Physician authorizations for medication changes
Individualized behavior plans in the Individualized Service Plan
Staff training records on this policy
QA/QI Committee minutes

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Plan (including HPN Communications)
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers, supervisors and the Administrator in the adult home / enriched housing program, ALR, EALR, SNALR and ALP
policies.purpose: To keep a DOH-approved written disaster and emergency plan, train everyone on it, and keep DOH informed through the Health Provider Network (HPN) so residents are protected in any emergency.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written disaster and emergency plan approved by DOH, submitted as part of the Part II application. The plan covers staff responsibilities, full and partial evacuation, preliminary relocation plans, coordination with community resources and local emergency planners, and plans for maintaining service with reduced personnel. Every new and current employee and volunteer is trained on the overall plan and on his or her own role. Staff performance is reviewed after each drill. Evacuation procedures are posted on every floor and in each wing, and emergency contact numbers and procedures are available to supervisory staff at all times. At least one staff person on each shift is designated to run an evacuation or the disaster plan. The Administrator keeps an HPN account with designated coordinators and users and a 24/7 emergency contact, and updates the HPN directory as changes occur and at least monthly. The Administrator notifies DOH by the next business day of any circumstance requiring implementation of the plan. The federal CMS emergency preparedness requirements for other provider types do not apply to this program; the state plan is the governing standard.

definitions.definition: The written plan approved by DOH that sets out how [AGENCY NAME] will protect residents in fires, severe weather, utility loss, infectious outbreaks, evacuations and similar events.
The DOH Health Provider Network, the secure system DOH uses to communicate with facilities and in which a 24/7 emergency contact must be maintained.
The person designated by [AGENCY NAME] to manage HPN accounts and users.
The staff person on each shift designated to run an evacuation or the disaster plan.

procedures: The Administrator will write the disaster and emergency plan before opening. It will address staff responsibilities, full and partial evacuation, preliminary relocation plans, coordination with community resources and local emergency planners, and maintaining service with reduced personnel. The Administrator will submit it to DOH with the Part II application and will not open until DOH approves it.

The Administrator will review the plan at least annually and after every drill, activation or change in the building, population or services. The Administrator will send each material change to the DOH regional office for approval before relying on it.
The Administrator will designate at least one staff person on every shift to run an evacuation or the disaster plan, and will list the designees on the posted schedule (see STF-01).

At hire and before working alone, each new employee and volunteer will be trained on the plan and on his or her own role. Current staff will be retrained at least annually and after any plan change. The Administrator will keep signed training records.
