The facility does not allow anyone to work whose condition endangers residents, themselves or others, or prevents them from doing their duties. In the ALR, the facility assesses and documents each employee's health status before the employee takes on resident care duties (10 NYCRR 1001.11(d)). For EALR/SNALR direct-care staff, immunization records, including rubella and measles immunity, are also kept (1001.11(q)). Health records are confidential.

definitions.definition: A signed statement from a physician (or a physician assistant or RN with special primary-care training working under physician oversight) who has physically examined the person, confirming no health impairment that would be a risk to residents or impede the person's duties.
A written evaluation of TB risk factors and current symptoms, combined with a TB test (skin test or FDA-approved blood assay).
TB infection without active disease. Treatment is facilitated and documented under the facility's policy.
Employees who provide hands-on care, supervision or services to residents.

procedures: As a condition of hire, the HR designee gives each applicant the health assessment forms. The offer is conditional on a satisfactory health statement and TB screening.

Before the employee works with residents, the HR designee collects a signed statement from a physician (or PA or RN with special primary-care training under physician oversight) who has physically examined the person. The statement must confirm that the person has no health impairment that is a risk to residents or would interfere with their duties. This is repeated at least every 12 months.

Before employment, each employee has a TB risk assessment, a symptom evaluation and a TB test (skin test or FDA-approved blood assay). The result is on file before resident contact begins, except as the regulation allows.
Each year, each employee completes a TB assessment that includes TB education, a risk assessment, and any follow-up tests indicated by the assessment. Records of education provided are kept.

Staff who have a positive TB test or symptoms of TB are referred promptly for clinical evaluation (e.g., chest X-ray and medical review). The Administrator receives only the work clearance and any restrictions, not diagnostic details.

The facility's policy on positive TB findings is that: an employee with active TB or suspected active TB does not work with residents until a licensed clinician documents they are not infectious; the facility facilitates and documents treatment of latent TB infection when recommended; and the facility reports to and follows the instructions of the local health department when required.
The HR designee also completes any additional tests required by the local board of health and keeps records.

If an employee has a documented religious exemption from required testing or immunization, the Administrator follows the documentation rules in 487.9(a)(9), keeps the written exemption on file, and applies any alternative precautions (such as symptom screening or mask use) directed by the health consultant or the local health department.

No person with a mental illness or substance habituation that endangers themselves or others, or prevents them from doing their duties, may work. If a supervisor has a concern, the supervisor immediately notifies the Administrator, who removes the person from resident contact and obtains a medical evaluation before return to work. The Administrator acts in line with civil rights and disability laws and consults counsel as needed.

No person with a communicable disease that endangers residents may work. Staff must report symptoms such as fever, vomiting, diarrhea, skin infection or a rash and are excluded from resident care until cleared, following SAF-07 and the health consultant's directions.

For the ALR, the Administrator documents the employee's health status assessment before the employee begins resident care duties. For EALR/SNALR direct-care staff, the HR designee also collects and files immunization records, including proof of rubella and measles immunity.

The HR designee keeps a tickler system listing every employee's annual health statement and TB assessment due dates. Notices go to employees 30 days before the due date. An employee whose statement is overdue by more than 30 days is removed from resident care until compliant.
Health records are kept in a confidential medical section of the personnel file, separate from general personnel records, and shared only as needed to protect residents and staff (STF-06).
The Administrator reports health compliance rates to the QA/QI Committee at least annually (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures no employee works without current clearance, removes employees who endanger residents and decides on exemptions and exclusions.
Collects, tracks and files health statements, TB results and immunization records and maintains due-date reminders.
Advises on TB policy, interprets results, supports follow-up and gives staff TB education.
Obtain required exams and tests, report symptoms and communicable disease and follow work restrictions.

documentation: Annual physician (or PA/RN) health statements
TB risk assessment, symptom evaluation and TB test results at hire and annually; TB education records
Policy on positive TB findings and records of latent TB treatment facilitation
Religious exemption documentation, if any
ALR pre-duty health status assessment
EALR/SNALR immunization records (rubella, measles)
Health due-date tracking report

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors and agency staff working in the Adult Home, Enriched Housing Program, ALR, EALR, SNALR and ALP
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, accurate and secure personnel record for every employee. The record must show that each person is qualified, healthy, screened, trained and paid correctly, and it must be ready for review by the Department of Health (DOH) at any time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains an individual personnel record and a separate payment record for every employee. Each personnel record contains verification of the required qualifications, the medical evaluation, and any incident reports involving the employee (18 NYCRR 487.9(a)(7)). Payment records contain all wages, benefits, reimbursements, bonuses, gifts and other payments. If the facility is subject to the Justice Center, each record also documents the Justice Center staff exclusion list check and the State Central Register check. Staff records, job descriptions, staffing schedules and payment records are kept as required by 18 NYCRR 487.10(d)(5)(vii). Staffing schedules are kept at least 12 months. Program and business records are retained 7 years (487.10(h)). Assisted Living Residence (ALR) personnel and training records are kept as required by the ALR regulations, including the training records required by 10 NYCRR 1001.11. For EALR and SNALR direct-care staff, immunization and TB records are included. HIV-related employee information is kept confidential and separate from the general file.

definitions.definition: The file for each employee holding qualification, screening, health, training, performance and incident documentation.
The record of all wages, benefits, reimbursements, bonuses, gifts or other payments made to an employee.
The Justice Center list of persons barred from working with vulnerable persons in covered facilities.
Any information indicating that a person has had an HIV test, has HIV infection or illness, or has been exposed to HIV. It must be kept in a separate, restricted file.

procedures: The Administrator designates a Personnel Records Custodian ([CUSTODIAN NAME]) who is responsible for creating, auditing and securing all personnel files.
Before an employee's first shift, the Custodian opens a personnel file containing the application, resume, interview notes, offer letter and signed job description.

The Custodian places in the file documentation verifying required qualifications: license or certificate, resident aide training certificate, first-aid or CPR credentials, reference checks, and proof that the employee can speak, read and write English.

Before the employee has unsupervised resident contact, the Custodian files the results of the Justice Center staff exclusion list check and State Central Register check (where the facility is subject to the Justice Center) and the criminal history background check. Dates and names of persons who ran each check are recorded.

The Custodian files the annual physician, physician assistant or registered nurse statement and the TB assessment as required by 18 NYCRR 487.9(a)(8). For EALR and SNALR direct-care staff, immunization and TB records are also filed. The Custodian tracks due dates and flags records 30 days before expiration.

Medical records and any HIV-related information are kept in a separate, locked file or restricted electronic folder. Only the Administrator, the Director of Nursing or designee, and the Custodian may access them. Disclosure follows RR-07.

The Custodian files orientation and in-service training records, including topics, dates, trainer and employee signature. For resident aides, the file shows the 40-hour initial training, 12 hours of annual in-service training, and the annual performance assessment with direct observation (10 NYCRR 1001.11).
The Custodian files the Justice Center code of conduct acknowledgment signed at hire and annually.
The Administrator or supervisor places in the file any incident report in which the employee was involved, along with the outcome, within 5 business days of the report.

Payroll maintains a separate payment record for each employee showing wages, benefits, reimbursements, bonuses, gifts and any other payments, and keeps it with or cross-referenced to the personnel record.
The Administrator keeps current written job descriptions for each position, and the Custodian files a signed copy in each employee's file.

Staffing schedules, as worked and as posted, are filed by week and kept at least 12 months. Staff records, job descriptions, schedules and payment records are kept as part of the facility's required records.

The Custodian audits all personnel files at least quarterly against a checklist, records deficiencies, and corrects them within 14 days. The Administrator reviews the audit results and reports them to the QA/QI Committee.

When an employee separates, the Custodian records the separation date and reason, closes the file, and retains program and business records for at least 7 years. Where a longer period applies under another law or program, the longer period governs.
Personnel files are stored in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. They are available to DOH on request, and access is logged.
Any request from an employee to review his or her own file is honored in the presence of the Custodian within a reasonable time. Requests are logged.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures records are complete and current, authorizes access, and reviews quarterly audit results.
Builds, audits, secures and retains files and tracks expiring items.
Maintains payment records and ensures they are linked to personnel records.
Submit incident reports, training sign-ins and performance assessments to the Custodian on time.

documentation: Personnel file checklist
Background check and Justice Center exclusion list/State Central Register verification
Medical evaluation and TB assessment
Training and orientation records
Payment records
Staffing schedules (kept 12 months)
Quarterly personnel record audit reports

policies.title: Staff Conduct, Professional Boundaries, Gratuities and Resident Work
policies.applies_to: All operators, administrators, employees, agents, volunteers and contractors; all residents who volunteer or are employed by the facility
policies.purpose: To set clear standards of conduct for everyone who works at [AGENCY NAME], protect residents from exploitation, and ensure that any resident work or volunteering is voluntary and lawful.
policies.policy: No operator, administrator, employee or agent of [AGENCY NAME] may accept any remuneration or gratuity from or on behalf of a resident for services, and residents may not be required to give gratuities (18 NYCRR 487.5(a)(3)(xvi), 487.5(d)(6)(ix)). A no-gratuity notice is posted in the facility. Staff must keep professional boundaries, treat residents with dignity, and follow the Justice Center code of conduct, which is given to and acknowledged by each employee at hire and annually (487.9(a)(3)(viii)). Staff must maintain clean, appropriate dress and hygiene and be emotionally, mentally and physically able to perform their duties (487.9(a)(12)). Residents may volunteer only without coercion or threats, not in place of required paid staff, and not in a way inconsistent with the resident's needs. Resident employment requires no coercion, fair compensation, and compliance with labor law. Written records are kept of each instance (487.9(b)).

definitions.definition: Any money, gift, favor, loan or thing of value given to or accepted by staff from a resident, a resident's family or representative, in connection with services.
The limit that separates a staff member's professional role from personal, financial, romantic or other relationships with a resident.
A resident who freely chooses to perform an uncompensated task for the facility or other residents.
A resident who is hired by the facility and paid for work in compliance with labor law.

procedures: The Administrator posts a notice in a public area stating that employees may not accept gratuities or remuneration, and checks monthly that it remains posted and legible.

At hire, each employee receives the Staff Conduct Policy and the Justice Center code of conduct, signs an acknowledgment, and the signed copy is filed in the personnel record. The acknowledgment is repeated annually.

During orientation, the trainer reviews professional boundaries, including prohibitions on accepting gifts or money, borrowing from or lending to residents, using resident property, personal social media contact, romantic or sexual relationships, and engaging in private business with residents.

A staff member offered a gift or money by a resident or family member declines politely, explains the policy, and reports the offer to the supervisor the same shift. The supervisor documents it on a Gratuity Offer Log. If the item cannot be returned immediately, the Administrator arranges return and records it.

A staff member who suspects a coworker has accepted a gratuity, exploited a resident, or crossed a boundary reports it to the Administrator immediately. Abuse, neglect or exploitation concerns are reported under SAF-01 and the Justice Center rules, in addition to this policy.

The Administrator reviews each report within 2 business days, interviews involved parties, and documents findings, corrective action and any discipline. Retaliation against a person who reports in good faith is prohibited.

Staff report to the supervisor any illness or condition that affects their ability to perform safely. The supervisor may send the employee home and documents the action. Staff must wear clean, appropriate attire and observe hygiene standards per the dress code.

Before any resident volunteers, the case manager or Administrator meets privately with the resident to confirm that the work is the resident's own free choice, that no one has threatened or pressured the resident, and that the work fits the resident's needs and abilities as shown in the assessment and service plan.
The Administrator confirms that volunteering does not replace any position required under the staffing schedule. Resident volunteers are never counted toward required staffing or supervision hours.
A resident volunteer may stop at any time without penalty. Refusal to volunteer has no effect on services, room, or continued residency.

If the facility proposes to employ a resident, the Administrator confirms that the resident consents freely, the rate and hours comply with applicable minimum wage and labor laws, and the resident is paid as other employees are paid. Payroll sets the resident up in the payroll system.

For each instance of volunteering or employment, the case manager records the resident's name, tasks, rate of pay (if employed) and hours in a Resident Work Record. The record is kept for each instance and reviewed monthly by the Administrator.
The case manager reviews each resident's volunteering or employment at least quarterly and at any change of condition, and stops it if it is inconsistent with the resident's needs.
The Administrator audits the Gratuity Offer Log, Resident Work Records and acknowledgment files quarterly and reports a summary to the QA/QI Committee.
Violations of this policy result in corrective action up to and including termination, and reports to the regional office, the Justice Center or other authorities as required.

responsibilities.duty: Posts notices, investigates reports, approves resident work arrangements and enforces discipline.
Screens resident volunteers and employees, completes Resident Work Records and reviews arrangements quarterly.
Receive gratuity offer reports, observe conduct, and send unfit staff home.
Follow the code of conduct, decline gratuities, keep boundaries and report violations.
Ensures any resident employee is paid in compliance with labor law.

documentation: Signed code of conduct acknowledgments (hire and annual)
No-gratuity notice posting checks
Gratuity Offer Log
Investigation and corrective action records
Resident Work Records (name, tasks, rate, hours)
Quarterly audit summaries

policies.title: Wages, Paid Sick Leave and Labor Law Compliance
policies.applies_to: All employees; ALP home care aides employed by the facility's licensed home care services agency (LHCSA); payroll and business office
federal: FLSA, 29 USC 201 et seq. (29 CFR 552 only for home care aides in an ALP LHCSA)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] pays every employee at least the legally required wage, provides paid sick leave, and meets its other wage and employment coverage obligations.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] pays no employee less than the New York minimum wage under Labor Law 652. From January 1, 2026 the rate is $17.00 per hour in New York City, Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester, and $16.00 per hour elsewhere in the State. These general rates stay the same on January 1, 2027. Aides employed by an ALP LHCSA who provide personal care are paid at least the home care aide minimum: $19.65 (NYC, Long Island, Westchester) and $18.65 (rest of State) in 2026, rising to $20.00 and $19.00 on January 1, 2027. Employees receive paid sick leave under Labor Law 196-b: 40 hours per year for employers with 5-99 employees and 56 hours for employers with 100 or more employees. [AGENCY NAME] also registers for New York unemployment insurance and carries workers' compensation, disability and paid family leave coverage. Payroll records are part of the personnel record system and are kept as set out in STF-06. Federal Fair Labor Standards Act overtime and recordkeeping rules apply, and the home care aide rules apply only to ALP LHCSA aides.

definitions.definition: The lowest hourly rate an employer may pay under Labor Law 652, which varies by region.
The higher minimum rate required for home care aides of a licensed home care services agency.

procedures: The Administrator identifies the facility's region (NYC/Long Island/Westchester or the rest of the State) and records it in the payroll file. The Administrator confirms the applicable general minimum wage each January.

Before January 1 each year, the Payroll Manager reviews every pay rate against the minimum wage for the coming year. Any rate below the minimum is raised effective January 1, and the change is documented.

The Payroll Manager identifies all employees of the ALP LHCSA who perform home care aide duties and verifies that they are paid at least the home care aide minimum ($19.65/$18.65 in 2026; $20.00/$19.00 from January 1, 2027).

The Administrator counts employees each calendar year to determine the sick leave tier (40 hours for 5-99 employees; 56 hours for 100 or more) and documents the count. If headcount changes the tier, the policy is updated and employees are notified.
The Payroll Manager sets up paid sick leave accrual in the payroll system and shows each employee's accrued and used balance on each pay statement or on request.

Employees request sick leave orally or in writing under the leave request procedure. The supervisor approves leave for the covered reasons without requiring unnecessary documentation, and does not retaliate against any employee for requesting or using it.
The Payroll Manager keeps the written Paid Sick Leave Policy and gives it to each employee at hire and when revised.

The Payroll Manager pays employees at least every pay period in compliance with Labor Law pay-frequency rules, issues wage statements, and pays overtime at one and one-half times the regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek as required by the FLSA and New York law.
At hire, the Payroll Manager gives each employee written notice of pay rate and pay day, as required by New York law, and keeps the signed copy in the personnel file.

Time is recorded by a timekeeping system or time sheets that capture all hours worked, including overnight and on-call time that is compensable. Supervisors do not alter time records without employee sign-off.

The Administrator confirms that the facility is registered for New York unemployment insurance and carries current workers' compensation, disability and paid family leave policies. The Administrator files the certificates and renewal dates in the business records and diarizes renewals 60 days ahead.
Resident employees are paid in compliance with this policy and with STF-07. The Payroll Manager verifies that each resident employee is paid at no less than the applicable minimum wage.

Each quarter, the Payroll Manager audits a sample of pay records for rate, overtime, sick leave accrual and record completeness and reports findings to the Administrator. Underpayments are corrected in the next pay period with back pay.
Payroll records are kept as part of personnel and business records and retained at least 7 years (see STF-06).

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All residents (Adult Home, Enriched Housing, ALR, EALR, SNALR and ALP); records staff, case managers, nursing, administration
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] creates, protects, keeps and retains a complete and accurate record for every resident, available to DOH staff and protected under privacy law.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a complete, accurate and current record for each resident in the facility and makes it available to DOH staff (18 NYCRR 487.10(c)). Each record contains a financial record (current admission agreement, payment account status, personal fund account, and inventory of property held) and a personal record (personal data, next of kin and emergency contact, medical and mental health evaluations, social evaluation summaries, referral details and correspondence). The facility uses the State-mandated forms, including DSS-2949 Personal Data Sheet, DSS-2900 Daily Census Record, DSS-3123 Incident Report, DSS-3122 Medical Evaluation, DSS-3027 Inventory of Resident Property, the personal allowance forms and the Mental Health Evaluation. A chronological admission and discharge register is kept. Individual resident records are retained at least 3 years after death or discharge. Program and business records are retained 7 years (487.10(h)). Resident records for ALR and ALP residents also meet the record requirements of the ALR regulations and ALP program rules. HIPAA-required policies and documentation are retained 6 years under 45 CFR 164.530(j). Where more than one period applies, the longer governs.

definitions.definition: The part of the resident record containing the admission agreement, payment account status, personal fund account and inventory of property.
The part of the resident record containing personal data, next of kin and emergency contacts, evaluations, social summaries, referral details and correspondence.
A chronological log of every admission and discharge, kept permanently as a facility record.

procedures: The Administrator designates a Medical Records Coordinator ([COORDINATOR NAME]) responsible for resident record content, security, access and retention.

On the day of admission, the Coordinator opens a record with a separate financial section and personal section, and enters the resident in the chronological admission and discharge register with the date and source of referral.

The admitting staff member completes the DSS-2949 Personal Data Sheet and records next of kin and emergency contacts. Contact details are verified with the resident and updated at least annually and at any change.

The Coordinator files in the personal record the DSS-3122 Medical Evaluation, the Mental Health Evaluation, social evaluation summaries, referral information and correspondence. Assessments, service plans and notes created under ARD-01 to ARD-03 are filed as they are completed.

The Business Office files in the financial record the current signed admission agreement, payment account status, the personal fund account, and the DSS-3027 Inventory of Resident Property. Resident property inventories are updated when property is added or removed, and the resident or representative signs.
Staff complete the DSS-2900 Daily Census Record every day, and the Incident Report DSS-3123 within the time set in SAF-02. Completed incident reports are filed according to policy.

All entries are legible, dated, timed where relevant, and signed with the staff member's name and title. Late entries are labeled as such. Errors are corrected by a single line and initialing, never by erasing or obliterating text.

Records are kept in a locked room or cabinet, or an access-controlled electronic system with audit logs. Only staff with a job-related need may access a record. Disclosure follows RR-07 (privacy, HIV-related information and HIPAA).

Current records are kept in the facility and are made available to DOH staff on request. Records are not removed from the facility except under a court order or as permitted by law, and electronic backups are maintained and tested at least quarterly.
The resident or the resident's legal representative may review the resident's record on request. The Coordinator schedules access within 2 business days and logs the request.
The Coordinator audits a sample of active records monthly for completeness, signatures, dates and required forms, and gives results to the Administrator for QA/QI review.
When a resident is discharged or dies, the Coordinator completes the register entry, closes the record within 30 days, and checks that financial settlement and property return are documented.

Closed individual resident records are retained for at least 3 years after the date of death or discharge. Program and business records (including quarterly rosters, financial statements and renewal materials) are retained 7 years. HIPAA policies and related documentation are retained 6 years. If the Medicaid program, litigation or an investigation requires a longer period, the Administrator extends retention.

Before destroying any record, the Administrator confirms the retention period has expired and no hold applies. Records are destroyed by shredding or secure electronic deletion, and a destruction log (record type, date range, date, method, person) is kept permanently.
If the facility closes or changes ownership, the Administrator follows GOV-07 to transfer or safely store records and notifies DOH of the storage location.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: Administrator, case manager, nursing and business office staff; all facility types and ALP
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] submits every required financial, statistical, incident and notice report to DOH and other State agencies completely and on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] meets all State reporting deadlines. The facility files the Annual Financial Statement DSS-2963 by the 15th day of the sixth calendar month after the fiscal year end, with an independent accountant's opinion when the capacity is 10 or more (18 NYCRR 487.10(e)(1)). It files the quarterly statistical information report and the quarterly resident roster with DOH (487.10(e)(2), (e)(5)). Facilities with 80 or more beds and 20 percent or more residents with serious mental illness file the additional quarterly and monthly reports (487.10(e)(3)-(4)). Incident-driven reports are made as follows: a resident death, attempted suicide or suspected felony is reported within 24 hours; a missing resident is reported the next working day with a written report in 5 working days (487.7(d)(4), (8)-(10)); and a reportable incident is reported to the Justice Center immediately on reasonable cause (487.14), with the follow-up report within 24 hours as required by 487.7(d)(14). The facility sends termination notices to the regional office within 5 days of service, files persistent-efforts reports every 90 days, notifies DOH within 3 business days of a key position vacancy, and notifies DOH by the next business day of a work stoppage, fire, loss of a fire system, no hot water or loss of essential services (487.12). ALR operators also file the annual quality measures and price reporting required by the Public Health Law.

definitions.definition: The Annual Financial Statement form filed by adult care facilities.

procedures: The Administrator maintains a Regulatory Reporting Calendar listing each report, due date, responsible person and submission method. The Calendar is reviewed at the start of each month and posted in the Administrator's office.

Within 45 days of fiscal year end, the Business Office begins the DSS-2963 and sends records to the independent accountant (if capacity is 10 or more). The Administrator reviews and signs the completed statement and submits it by the 15th day of the sixth calendar month after fiscal year end. The submission confirmation is filed.

Within the first 10 days after each calendar quarter ends, the Administrator prepares the quarterly statistical information report and quarterly resident roster from the census records and submits them to DOH by the due date. The Business Office checks them against the Daily Census Records.

If the facility has 80 or more beds and 20 percent or more residents with serious mental illness, the Administrator identifies the additional quarterly and monthly reports, assigns each to a named staff member and adds the dates to the Calendar.

When a resident dies, attempts suicide, or a suspected felony occurs, the supervisor on duty notifies the Administrator immediately. The Administrator or designee reports to the required authority within 24 hours, records who was notified, the date and time, and completes the Incident Report DSS-3123.
When a resident is missing, staff follow SAF-03. The Administrator notifies DOH by the next working day and submits the written report within 5 working days.

Any employee with reasonable cause to suspect a reportable incident reports it to the Justice Center immediately, and the Administrator starts the facility's investigation. The Justice Center-related written report is completed within 24 hours as required, and the call confirmation number is recorded.

When a termination (involuntary discharge) notice is served on a resident, the Administrator sends a copy to the regional office within 5 days of service and files proof of mailing or transmission (see ARD-05).

While persistent efforts to secure an appropriate placement for a resident are required, the case manager prepares the persistent-efforts report every 90 days. The Administrator submits it to the regional office and keeps a copy.

When a key position becomes vacant, the Administrator notifies the regional office in writing within 3 business days. The Administrator records the vacancy date, notice date, interim coverage plan and fill date (see STF-01).

When a work stoppage, fire, loss of a fire protection system, loss of hot water or loss of any essential service occurs, the Administrator or the highest-ranking person on duty notifies DOH by the next business day and documents the notice (see SAF-05 and SAF-06).

For an ALR, the Administrator prepares the annual quality measures and price reporting required by the Public Health Law, and the Business Office updates the public price information at the same time (see REC-03).

The Administrator or designee keeps a copy of every report with proof of delivery (system confirmation, certified mail receipt or email transmission) in the regulatory reports file for at least 7 years.
If a deadline cannot be met, the Administrator contacts the regional office or the appropriate DOH bureau before the due date, documents the reason and submits the report as soon as possible.
Each quarter, the Administrator reports to the QA/QI Committee on timeliness of required reports, any late filings and corrective actions.

policies.title: Posting of Required Documents and Notices
policies.applies_to: Administrator and all staff; all public and resident areas of the facility, and the facility website (ALR)
policies.purpose: To make sure residents, families, staff and visitors can see the documents, notices and phone numbers that State law requires [AGENCY NAME] to post.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] posts the following in a conspicuous place accessible to residents and visitors (18 NYCRR 487.10(g)): the operating certificate; the latest inspection report and follow-up reports; the statement of resident rights; weekly menus; the monthly activities schedule; evacuation procedures; the notice prohibiting employee gratuities; the schedule of times when residents may access their personal allowance accounts; and the procedures for presenting grievances. If the facility is subject to the Justice Center, it posts the Justice Center hotline number where residents, staff, volunteers and contractors can see it (487.5(c)). The facility also posts DOH's Adult Care Facility complaint line, 1-866-893-6772 (Social Services Law 460-d). ALRs also post the starting monthly rate, rent range, approved residency agreement and fee summary, both on the website and in the facility. Evacuation procedures are posted on every floor and in each wing. All postings are current, legible and at a height and location that residents with mobility, vision or language needs can access.

definitions.definition: A location in a common area that residents and visitors regularly pass, where a notice can be easily seen and read.
The State hotline for reporting abuse, neglect and other reportable incidents involving vulnerable persons.
The DOH adult care facility complaint number, 1-866-893-6772.
A written list of every required posting, its location and the date of last verification.

procedures: The Administrator appoints a Posting Coordinator ([COORDINATOR NAME]) to maintain the Required Postings Checklist and the posting board locations.
The Posting Coordinator posts the operating certificate in the main entrance or other public area and replaces it immediately when DOH issues a new or amended certificate.

When DOH issues an inspection report, the Administrator posts it within 2 business days of receipt, together with any plan of correction or follow-up report. Reports are kept posted until replaced by the next inspection report and follow-up documents.
The Posting Coordinator posts the statement of resident rights (see RR-01) in a common area. Copies in languages spoken by residents and in large print are posted or made available (see RR-08).

The Dietary Manager gives the weekly menu to the Posting Coordinator by [DAY/TIME] each week, and it is posted before the start of the menu week. The Activities Director gives the monthly activities schedule by the 25th of the preceding month, and it is posted before the first of the month.

The Posting Coordinator posts the evacuation procedures on every floor and in each wing, with route maps showing the viewer's location, and updates them after any change of layout or procedure (see SAF-06).
The Posting Coordinator posts the notice prohibiting employee gratuities (see STF-07) in a public area.
The Business Office provides the schedule of times when residents may access their personal allowance accounts (see RR-05). The Posting Coordinator posts it and replaces it when the schedule changes.
The Posting Coordinator posts the grievance procedure (see RR-02) naming the person to receive grievances, and the Ombudsman contact information (see RR-03).

If the facility is subject to the Justice Center, the Posting Coordinator posts the Justice Center hotline number in places visible to residents, staff, volunteers and contractors, including at least one staff area.
The Posting Coordinator posts the DOH ACF complaint line, 1-866-893-6772, next to the resident rights statement and grievance procedure.

For an ALR, the Administrator posts in the facility, and the Business Office publishes on the facility website, the starting monthly rate, the rent range, the approved residency agreement and the fee summary. They are updated within 5 business days of any change approved or required by DOH.

Postings are placed at a height and in a format that residents who use wheelchairs or have low vision can read. For residents who cannot read the postings, case managers explain them at admission and annually.

The Posting Coordinator inspects every posting weekly and completes the Required Postings Checklist with date, initials and any replaced item. Missing, outdated, torn or illegible postings are replaced within 1 business day.
The Administrator reviews the checklist monthly and before any DOH survey, keeps checklist copies for at least 3 years, and reports any lapses to the QA/QI Committee.
